chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Kurdawayh, who said:
I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a well into which rainwater enters, containing urine, feces, the urine of beasts, their dung, and the droppings of dogs.
He said: Thirty buckets should be drawn from it.

And even if it is malodorous, this report does not conflict with what we specified regarding drawing fifty buckets, because this report is specific to rainwater with which one of these impure things becomes mixed and then enters the well. In that case, its use is permissible after drawing forty buckets. And the report we cited earlier applies to when the feces itself falls into the well, so there is no contradiction between them in any way.

key_terms.اسْتِعْمَالُهُ: its use, meaning the permissibility of using the well water after prescribed removal
key_terms.النَّجَاسَاتِ: ritually impure substances that affect the ruling of the water
key_terms.الْعَذِرَةُ: feces/filth considered among the impurities mentioned
key_terms.بِئْرٍ: a well whose water is being discussed in the legal ruling
key_terms.ثَلَاثُونَ دَلْوًا: thirty buckets, the quantity specified in the narration
key_terms.خَمْسِينَ دَلْوًا: fifty buckets, the quantity mentioned in another reconciled report
key_terms.مَاءُ الْمَطَرِ: rainwater that enters the well while mixed with impurities
key_terms.يُنْزَحُ: it should be drawn out, referring to removing water from the well

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a well contaminated by rainwater mixed with najasah in al-Istibṣār?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of a well contaminated by rainwater mixed with impurities such as urine and feces. It states that a set number of buckets should be drawn out, and then reconciles this report with another narration by distinguishing between impurity entering through mixed rainwater and the impurity itself falling directly into the well.
